sections.english: Say to yourself first thing in the morning: today I shall meet people who are meddling, ungrateful, aggressive, treacherous, malicious, unsocial. All this has afflicted them through their ignorance of true good and evil. But I have seen that the nature of good is what is right, and the nature of evil what is wrong; and I have reflected that the nature of the offender himself is akin to my own — not a kinship of blood or seed, but a sharing in the same mind, the same fragment of divinity. Therefore I cannot be harmed by any of them, as none will infect me with their wrong. Nor can I be angry with my kinsman or hate him. We were born for cooperation, like feet, like hands, like eyelids, like the rows of upper and lower teeth. So to work in opposition to one another is against nature: and anger or rejection is opposition.
sections.chinese: 清晨即起，当自谓曰：今日我将遇好管闲事之人、忘恩负义之人、蛮横无礼之人、奸诈狡猾之人、心怀恶意之人、落落寡合之人。凡此种种，皆因其不识真善真恶之故。然我已洞见：善之本质在于其正，恶之本质在于其邪；我亦沉思，冒犯者之本性实与我同源——非血亲或种嗣之亲，乃共享同一理性、同禀一分神性之亲。故无人能损我分毫，因无人能将其罪愆染及我身。我亦不能对同源之人动怒或怀恨。吾辈生而为协作，犹如双足，犹如双手，犹如眼睑，犹如上下齿列。故彼此相悖而行，乃逆自然之道：愤怒与排斥，即是相悖。

sections.english: Whatever it is, this being of mine is made up of flesh, breath, and directing mind. Now the flesh you should disdain — blood, bones, a mere fabric and network of nerves, veins, and arteries. Consider too what breath is: wind — and not even a constant, but all the time being disgorged and sucked in again. That leaves the third part, the directing mind. Quit your books — no more hankering: this is not your gift. No, think like this, as if you were on the point of death: 'you are old; don't then let this directing mind of yours be enslaved any longer — no more jerking to the strings of selfish impulse, no more disquiet at your present or suspicion of your future fate.'
sections.chinese: 无论如何，我之此身，乃由血肉、气息与主宰之心灵所构成。至于血肉，你当鄙薄之——血、骨，无非神经、静脉与动脉之织物与网络。再思气息为何物：风而已矣——且非恒常之风，不过时时呼出复又吸入者也。所余者，第三部分：主宰之心灵。放下你的书卷——不复眷恋：此非你所禀赋。不若如此思之，如你即将赴死：「你已年迈；勿再令此主宰之心灵受奴役——勿再为自私冲动之绳线所牵曳，勿再对当下惴惴不安，勿再对将来之命运满腹狐疑。」

sections.english: The works of the gods are full of providence. The works of Fortune are not independent of Nature or the spinning and weaving together of the threads governed by Providence. All things flow from that world: and further factors are necessity and the benefit of the whole universe, of which you are a part. Now every part of nature benefits from that which is brought by the nature of the Whole and all which preserves that nature: and the order of the universe is preserved equally by the changes in the elements and the changes in their compounds. Let this be enough for you, and your constant doctrine. And give up your thirst for books, so that you do not die a grouch, but in true grace and heartfelt gratitude to the gods.
sections.chinese: 诸神之作为充满天意。命运之作为亦非独立于自然，亦非独立于天意所掌之经纬交织。万物皆自彼世涌流而来：且更有必然性与整个宇宙之福祉——你为其一部分。自然之每一部分皆受益于整体自然之所赐，受益于一切维系此自然之物：宇宙之秩序同样赖元素之变化及其复合物之变化而得以维持。此理于你当为足够，当作你恒常之道。且放下求书若渴之心，如此你方能不于怨愤中离世，而于真正之从容中对诸神满怀感激。

sections.english: Remember how long you have been putting this off, how many times you have been given a period of grace by the gods and not used it. It is high time now for you to understand the universe of which you are a part, and the governor of that universe of whom you constitute an emanation: and that there is a limit circumscribed to your time — if you do not use it to clear away your clouds, it will be gone, and you will be gone, and the opportunity will not return.
sections.chinese: 记取你已将此推迟多久，诸神曾予你多少缓冲之时日而你未曾利用。如今正是时候，你当领悟你身为其一部分之宇宙，领悟你作为其流溢之宇宙主宰：且悟你的时间有一限界——若你不用之以驱散你心中之迷雾，则时间将逝，你亦将逝，而良机不再。

sections.english: Every hour of the day give vigorous attention, as a Roman and as a man, to the performance of the task in hand with precise analysis, with unaffected dignity, with human sympathy, with dispassionate justice — and to vacating your mind from all its other thoughts. And you will achieve this vacation if you perform each action as if it were the last of your life: freed, that is, from all lack of aim, from all passion-led deviation from the ordinance of reason, from pretence, from love of self, from dissatisfaction with what fate has dealt you. You see how few things a man needs to master for the settled flow of a god-fearing life. The gods themselves ask nothing more of one who keeps these observances.
sections.chinese: 一日之中，每时每刻，当如罗马人，如堂堂男子，以精审之分析、不由矫饰之尊严、人之同情、不动于情之公正，专心致志于手头之务——并使心灵从一切杂念中抽身而出。你若将每一行动当作生命之最后一举来施行，便能成就此等放空：即，从一切目标缺失中解脱，从一切由激情驱使而违理性训令之偏轨中解脱，从虚伪中解脱，从自恋中解脱，从对命运所予之不满中解脱。你看，一个人需要掌控之事何其少也，便能获致虔敬生命之安流。诸神于恪守此等训诫者，亦别无他求。

sections.english: Self-harm, my soul, you are doing self-harm: and you will have no more opportunity for self-respect. Life for each of us is a mere moment, and this life of yours is nearly over, while you still show yourself no honour, but let your own welfare depend on other people's souls. Do externals tend to distract you? Then give yourself the space to learn some further good lesson, and stop your wandering. That done, you must guard against the other sort of drift. Those who are dead to life and have no aim for the direction of every impulse and, more widely, every thought are drivellers in deed as well as word.
sections.chinese: 自伤也，吾之魂灵，你在行自伤之事：而你不再有自我尊重之机。于我等每人而言，生命不过一瞬，而你此生已近尾声，你犹未示己以尊重，却令一己之福祉依赖于他人之魂灵。身外之物岂易使你分心？那便予自己空间，学取更多良训，止住你的游荡。此事既成，你当慎防另一种飘移。那些于生命已死、无一目标以引导每一冲动、乃至每一思想之人，不唯言辞，即其行事，亦不过是口涎横流之徒。

sections.english: Failure to read what is happening in another's soul is not easily seen as a cause of unhappiness: but those who fail to attend to the motions of their own soul are necessarily unhappy.
sections.chinese: 未能洞悉他人魂灵之所历，不易被视为不幸之因：然未能关注自身魂灵之动作者，其不幸乃是必然。

sections.english: Always remember these things: what the nature of the Whole is, what my own nature is, the relation of this nature to that, what kind of part it is of what kind of Whole; and that there is no one who can prevent you keeping all that you say and do in accordance with that nature, of which you are a part.
sections.chinese: 当时刻铭记此等事理：整体之自然为何，我自身之自然为何，此自然与彼自然之关系如何，此一部分在何种整体中居于何种位置；且铭记，无人能阻挡你使你一切言行符合于你为其一部分之自然。

sections.english: In his comparative ranking of sins, applying philosophy to the common man's distinctions, Theophrastus says that offences of lust are graver than those of anger: because it is clearly some sort of pain and involuntary spasm which drives the angry man to abandon reason, whereas the lust-led offender has given in to pleasure and seems somehow more abandoned and less manly in his wrongdoing. Rightly, then, and like a true philosopher, Theophrastus said that greater censure attaches to an offence committed under the influence of pleasure than to one under the influence of pain. And in general the one is more like an injured party, forced to anger by the pain of provocation: whereas the other is his own source of the impulse to wrong, driven to what he does by lust.
sections.chinese: 泰奥弗拉斯图斯在比较罪行之轻重时，将哲学运用于常人之区分，谓欲望之罪重于愤怒之罪：因驱使愤怒者抛弃理性者，显然为某种痛苦与非自愿之痉挛，而受欲望驱使而犯罪者，乃屈服于快乐，于其过犯中似更为放纵、更失丈夫气概。故泰奥弗拉斯图斯如真正哲学家一般，正确指出：受快乐影响而犯之罪，比之受痛苦影响而犯之罪，更当受谴责。概而言之，前者更似受伤之一方，为挑衅之痛苦所逼而怒；后者则自身即为作恶冲动之源，为其欲望所驱而为之。

sections.english: You may leave this life at any moment: have this possibility in your mind in all that you do or say or think. Now departure from the world of men is nothing to fear, if gods exist: because they would not involve you in any harm. If they do not exist, or if they have no care for humankind, then what is life to me in a world devoid of gods, or devoid of providence? But they do exist, and they do care for humankind: and they have put it absolutely in man's power to avoid falling into the true kinds of harm. If there were anything harmful in the rest of experience, they would have provided for that too, to make it in everyone's power to avoid falling into it; and if something cannot make a human being worse, how could it make his life a worse life? The nature of the Whole would not have been blind to this, either through ignorance or with knowledge unaccompanied by the power to prevent and put right. Nor would it have made so great an error, through lack of power or skill, as to have good and bad falling indiscriminately, on good and bad people alike. Yes, death and life, fame and ignominy, pain and pleasure, wealth and poverty — all these come to good and bad alike, but they are not in themselves either right or wrong: neither then are they inherent good or evil.
sections.chinese: 你随时可能辞别此生：凡所行、所言、所思，心中皆当存此一念。若诸神存在，离开人世便无所可惧：因诸神必不陷你于任何伤害。若诸神不存在，或于人类漠不关心，则我居于此无神、无天意之世，生命又有何义？然诸神确实存在，且关切人类：彼等已将避免陷入真正之伤害的能力，全然置于人之掌控中。若其余经验中尚有危害之物，彼等亦必为之预备，使人皆能避免坠入其中；若某物不能使人变恶，又如何能使人之生命变恶？整体之自然必不致对此视而不见——或出于无知，或虽有知而无能预防与纠正。亦不致因力量或技巧之欠缺，而犯如此大错，以至善恶无别地降临于善人与恶人之身。诚然，死与生、荣与辱、苦与乐、富与贫——凡此种种，善人恶人皆同样遭遇，然其本身既非正亦非邪：故亦非固有之善或固有之恶。

sections.english: How all things quickly vanish, our bodies themselves lost in the physical world, the memories of them lost in time; the nature of all objects of the senses — especially those which allure us with pleasure, frighten us with pain, or enjoy the applause of vanity — how cheap they are, how contemptible, shoddy, perishable, and dead: these are matters for our intellectual faculty to consider. And further considerations. What are they, these people whose judgements and voices confer or deny esteem? What is death? Someone looking at death per se, and applying the analytical power of his mind to divest death of its associated images, will conclude then that it is nothing more than a function of nature — and if anyone is frightened of a function of nature, he is a mere child. And death is not only a function of nature, but also to her benefit. Further. How does man touch god, with what part of his being, and when that part of him is in what sort of disposition?
sections.chinese: 万物何其速朽也——吾辈之躯体消失于物质世界中，其记忆湮灭于时间之中；感官对象之本质——尤其那些以快乐诱人、以痛苦恐吓人、或享有虚荣喝彩之物——何其廉价、何其可鄙、何其粗劣、易逝而枯死：此皆吾辈智识官能所当思虑者也。更有进者：那些以判断和声音赋予或剥夺尊敬者，究竟是何等人？死亡为何物？有人直视死亡本身，运用心智之分析力剥离死亡之种种联想意象，便将断言：死亡无非自然之一种功用——而若有人对自然之一种功用感到恐惧，那便是孩童无疑。且死亡不仅是自然之一种功用，亦有益于自然。更有进者：人如何触及神，以己身之哪一部分，且该部分处于何种境地之时？

sections.english: Nothing is more miserable than one who is always out and about, running round everything in circles — in Pindar's words 'delving deep in the bowels of the earth' — and looking for signs and symptoms to divine his neighbours' minds. He does not realize that it is sufficient to concentrate solely on the divinity within himself and to give it true service. That service is to keep it uncontaminated by passion, triviality, or discontent at what is dealt by gods or men. What comes from the gods demands reverence for their goodness. What comes from men is welcome for our kinship's sake, but sometimes pitiable also, in a way, because of their ignorance of good and evil: and this is no less a disability than that which removes the distinction of light and dark.
sections.chinese: 世间最可怜者，莫过于终日在外奔走，绕一切事物团团转——如品达所谓「深掘大地之脏腑」——寻迹觅兆以揣测邻人之心意。彼浑然不知，专注其一己内心之神性并予以真正事奉，便已足够。此事奉即是保持其神性不为激情、琐屑，或对神人之所赐所予心怀不满所污染。自诸神中来者，需对其善德怀敬畏之心。自众人中来者，因吾辈之同源关系而欣然接纳，然有时亦以某种方式令人怜悯，因其对善恶之无知：此等残疾，不减于令人不辨光明与黑暗者。

sections.english: Even if you were destined to live three thousand years, or ten times that long, nevertheless remember that no one loses any life other than the one he lives, or lives any life other than the one he loses. It follows that the longest and the shortest lives are brought to the same state. The present moment is equal for all; so what is passing is equal also; the loss therefore turns out to be the merest fragment of time. No one can lose either the past or the future — how could anyone be deprived of what he does not possess? So always remember these two things. First, that all things have been of the same kind from everlasting, coming round and round again, and it makes no difference whether one will see the same things for a hundred years, or two hundred years, or for an infinity of time. Second, that both the longest-lived and the earliest to die suffer the same loss. It is only the present moment of which either stands to be deprived: and if indeed this is all he has, he cannot lose what he does not have.
sections.chinese: 纵使你命中注定活上三千年，或十倍于彼，仍当铭记：无人能失去他所活过之外的任何生命，也无人能活出他所失去之外的任何生命。由此推论，最长与最短之生命皆归于同一状态。当下此刻，人人均等；故所逝去者亦均等；所失者原来不过是时间之最微片段。无人能失去过去或未来——人焉能被剥夺其所不拥有之物？故当时刻谨记此二事：其一，万物自永恒以来便属同类，循环往复而来，人之所见，百年、二百年、或无穷时间，并无分别。其二，最长寿者与最早夭者所失相同。二者所将被剥夺者，唯此当下此刻：且若此确为其所有之全部，则其不能失去其所无有。

sections.english: 'All is as thinking makes it so.' The retort made to Monimus the Cynic is clear enough: but clear too is the value of his saying, if one takes the kernel of it, as far as it is true.
sections.chinese: 「一切皆如思之所示。」对犬儒莫尼摩斯之反驳，自是显而易见：然若取其核心要义，以其真实所及为限，则其言之价值亦同样显然。

sections.english: The soul of a man harms itself, first and foremost, when it becomes (as far as it can) a separate growth, a sort of tumour on the universe: because to resent anything that happens is to separate oneself in revolt from Nature, which holds in collective embrace the particular natures of all other things. Secondly, when it turns away from another human being, or is even carried so far in opposition as to intend him harm — such is the case in the souls of those gripped by anger. A soul harms itself, thirdly, when it gives in to pleasure or pain. Fourthly, whenever it dissimulates, doing or saying anything feigned or false. Fifthly, whenever it fails to direct any of its own actions or impulses to a goal, but acts at random, without conscious attention — whereas even the most trivial action should be undertaken in reference to the end. And the end for rational creatures is to follow the reason and the rule of that most venerable archetype of a governing state — the Universe.
sections.chinese: 人之灵魂自损，第一且最甚者，当其变为（尽其可能地）一种分离之赘生物，如宇宙上之肿囊：因怨恨所发生之任何事，即是反叛自然，与自然分离——自然本将所有其他事物之特殊本性统抱于怀。其次，当其背离另一人，或甚至在对立之中至于意欲害人——此乃为愤怒所攫之灵魂中之情状。灵魂自损，第三，当其屈服于快乐或痛苦。第四，当其伪饰，做出或说出任何假装或虚假之事。第五，当其未能指引自身任何行动或冲动朝向一目标，而是漫无目的地行动，无所知觉——然而即便是最为琐碎之举，亦当参照终极目的而行事。而理性造物之终极目的，即是遵循理性，遵循那最为庄严之治理邦国之原型——宇宙——的法则。

sections.english: In man's life his time is a mere instant, his existence a flux, his perception fogged, his whole bodily composition rotting, his mind a whirligig, his fortune unpredictable, his fame unclear. To put it shortly: all things of the body stream away like a river, all things of the mind are dreams and delusion; life is warfare, and a visit in a strange land; the only lasting fame is oblivion. What then can escort us on our way? One thing, and one thing only: philosophy. This consists in keeping the divinity within us inviolate and free from harm, master of pleasure and pain, doing nothing without aim, truth, or integrity, and independent of others' action or failure to act. Further, accepting all that happens and is allotted to it as coming from that other source which is its own origin: and at all times awaiting death with the glad confidence that it is nothing more than the dissolution of the elements of which every living creature is composed. Now if there is nothing fearful for the elements themselves in their constant changing of each into another, why should one look anxiously in prospect at the change and dissolution of them all? This is in accordance with nature: and nothing harmful is in accordance with nature.
sections.chinese: 人之生命中，其时不过一瞬，其存在不过一潮流，其知觉蒙雾不清，其全部身体组织正在腐朽，其心灵如旋转之陀螺，其命运不可预测，其名声晦暗不明。简而言之：躯体之一切如河水奔逝，心灵之一切皆梦幻与虚妄；生命是战场，亦是异乡之旅；唯一持久之名乃是遗忘。然则，何物能伴我们行路？一事，唯此一事：哲学。此即是：保持吾辈内心之神性不受侵犯、不为所害，做苦乐之主宰，无事不怀目的、真理与正直而行，独立于他人之行动或不行动。更有进者，接纳所发生及所分配于己之一切，视其为源自另一源头——亦即其自身之源起：并时时心怀喜悦之确信等待死亡，知死亡不过是构成每一生灵之元素的分解而已。既然元素本身在彼此不断转化之中无所畏怖，则人何以要对这一切之变化与分解心怀焦虑？此乃符合自然之道：而凡符合自然之道者，皆非有害。
